newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-NICARAGUA SEEKS ENTRY INTO CARIBBEAN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-NICARAGUA SEEKS ENTRY INTO CARIBBEAN SERIES.

text.p: Nicaragua wants to join the four-nation Caribbean Series baseball tournament and bring Cuba along with it, Nicaraguan baseball officials said Saturday.
The Caribbean Series, currently underway in this northern Mexican city, features professional winter league champions of Mexico, Venezuela, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic.

Nicaragua has asked the Caribbean Professional Baseball Confederation, which runs the series, to become a full member of the confederation with the idea of later competing in the championship. Because the series needs an even number of teams, Nicaragua proposed that Cuba join as well.

Baseball is a national passion in Nicaragua, but its top league has mostly amateur players, allowing just four foreign professionals per team. The Caribbean Series usually features teams filled with Major League and minor league professionals.

"I think that if Nicaragua is accepted in the Caribbean Series, we're going to bring Cuba along," Carlos Garcia, president of the Nicaraguan Baseball Federation, told reporters. "Cuba is ready. The only problem is of a political order."

Although Cuba has not sought entrance on it own, Nicaraguan officials said it was the logical nation to join because of its high level of play. Cuba, which dominates international amateur competition and boasts major league calibre talent, won its second consecutive Olympic gold medal in Atlanta last summer.
Some members, notably Puerto Rico, object to Nicaraguan entry because they consider the level of play there to be inferior.
Confederation directors are expected to vote on Nicaragua's membership request on Sunday.
